questions.subtopic: A Day at the Animal Shelter (Y6-109)
questions.learningFocus: Reading: A Day at the Animal Shelter
questions.passage: A Day at the Animal Shelter. Last weekend, my family and I volunteered at the Sunshine Animal Shelter near our hometown. The shelter takes care of abandoned dogs and cats. When we arrived, the manager, Ms. Tan, gave us a tour. We learned that the shelter has been running for fifteen years and is funded mostly by donations. Our first job was to feed the animals. We measured out the right portions of dry food for each dog. After that, we walked some of the dogs in the garden. My favourite moment was when I helped wash a puppy named Brownie. Brownie was rescued from a drain a month ago. Now she is happy and healthy. I left the shelter feeling grateful and inspired. I plan to visit again next month.

The Old Library. Our school has an old library that has been used for over forty years. Recently, the headmaster announced plans to renovate it. The library will get new shelves, a reading corner with bean bags, and a digital catalog. Students are encouraged to donate old books they no longer read. Some parents have offered to paint the walls and donate bookshelves. The librarian, Mr. Ravi, said the renovation will take about three months. During the renovation, students can borrow books from the temporary library in the hall. Everyone is excited about the new look. We hope the renovation will encourage more students to read regularly.

My Grandmother's Garden. My grandmother lives in a small village in Perak. Behind her wooden house, there is a beautiful garden filled with flowers and fruit trees. The garden has been there for decades. Every morning, my grandmother waters the plants with water from the well. She also talks to them softly, saying they grow better when spoken to nicely. She grows starfruit, mango, and guava trees. The vegetables she grows include lady's fingers, long beans, and chillies. When I visit during school holidays, I help her weed and water the garden. She always rewards me with fresh fruit for my help. I learn a lot from her, especially how to care for nature.

The garden has been there for decades. Every morning, my grandmother waters the plants with water from the well. She also talks to them softly, saying they grow better when spoken to nicely. She grows starfruit, mango, and guava trees. The vegetables she grows include lady's fingers, long beans, and chillies. When I visit during school holidays, I help her weed and water the garden. She always rewards me with fresh fruit for my help. I learn a lot from her, especially how to care for nature.

The prize was a school trip to the recycling factory in Shah Alam. During the trip, we learned how recycled materials are sorted, cleaned, and turned into new products. We saw stacks of newspapers becoming fresh paper. We also learned that one recycled aluminium can save enough energy to run a television for three hours. The competition taught us the value of recycling and we plan to do it every year.

Chef Amin emphasized the importance of using fresh ingredients and avoiding too much oil. At the end of the class, we received a certificate and a small recipe book. I really enjoyed the class because I learned cooking skills that I can use at home. I plan to help my mother cook dinner this week.

questions.passage: The Visit to the Hospital. Last Friday, my class went on a visit to the government hospital to learn about healthcare. We met Dr. Wong, who showed us around the paediatric ward. She explained that doctors and nurses work as a team to take care of sick children. We saw how patients received medicine and how nurses monitored their progress. One of the highlights was when we were allowed to visit the children's playroom, where toys and books were available. We spent time playing with the children, which brightened their day. Before leaving, Dr. Wong reminded us to wash our hands often to stay healthy. The visit taught us the importance of healthcare workers.

questions.passage: The Pen-Pal Exchange Programme. Our school recently started a pen-pal exchange programme with a school in Sabah. Students in Year 5 and Year 6 were invited to participate. We each received a name and address of a student from the other school. We wrote letters introducing ourselves, our hobbies, and our families. After two weeks, we received replies from our pen-pals. Reading the letters was exciting because I learned about life in a different part of Malaysia. My pen-pal, Dania, lives near a river and enjoys fishing. She told me about local foods like hinava and tuhau. We plan to exchange letters every month. The programme has broadened my perspective on Malaysian culture.

The Mountain Hike. Last Saturday, my family and I went hiking at Bukit Tabur in Selangor. We started the hike at 7 a.m. The trail was quite steep and rocky, so we had to be careful. Halfway up, we stopped at a small waterfall and drank fresh water. The view from the top was breathtaking. We could see the entire city below us and the mountains in the distance. The hike took about four hours to complete. We felt proud of ourselves for reaching the summit. The descent was even more challenging, but we took our time and arrived safely. The hike taught us to value teamwork and perseverance.

questions.passage: My First Job: Newspaper Delivery. When I was 12, my parents allowed me to take on a small job delivering newspapers in our neighbourhood. Every morning, I had to wake up at 5 a.m. to fold the newspapers and deliver them to my customers before 6.30 a.m. It was tough at first, especially during rainy days when I had to keep the papers dry. However, I learned to be responsible and to manage my time well. My customers appreciate the prompt delivery. Each month, I earn RM80 from the newspaper company, which I save for a new bicycle. My parents are proud of my hard work and dedication. I plan to continue this job until I finish secondary school.

questions.passage: The Picnic at the Beach. Last weekend, my family and I had a picnic at Port Dickson beach. We left home at 6 a.m. to avoid the traffic. The beach was clean and not too crowded. My mother had prepared sandwiches, fruits, and cold drinks for the picnic. My father set up the mat and umbrella while my brother and I played in the sand. I swam in the shallow water and collected seashells. Around noon, we had a delicious lunch under the umbrella. After lunch, we took a walk along the shore and watched the waves. The cool breeze made the day very enjoyable. We returned home at 5 p.m., tired but happy. It was the best weekend of my life.
